newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen staying flat this week.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen staying flat this week.

text.p: Polish shares fell after Friday's gain but analysts saw growth on Tuesday and said the market would extend last week's relatively flat performance after recent sharper moves.
The market had surged about 38 percent this year before falling 4.7 percent over four sessions at the turn of February and March.

"In the course of the stabilisation phase investors with a view on the coming market trend will take positions and then we'll see if there's more supply or demand, probably at this week's end," said Artur Czerwonski of Bank Pekao SA brokerage.
The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.6 percent to 17,596.1 points and turnover fell 23.7 percent to 180.3 million zlotys on all three markets.
Analysts said potential growth of small-cap stocks which did well last week, such as Relpol, and current rises by computer firms Optimus and ComputerLand, could push the overall market up this week.

They said that though larger investors were slowing buying after big blue-chip gains this year the main market, with a price-earnings ratio around 16, did not necessarily look expensive compared to other emerging markets.

Analysts said Monday's news that food prices were flat in the last 10 days of February and had risen 0.1 percent since the last ten days of January would cheer the market even though no interest rate cut was anticipated.
Large-cap Debica was the main market's biggest loser on Monday, down 4.7 percent.

Analysts said top gainer Kredyt Bank, up 4.1 percent, may have been helped by a price-to-book ratio less than half the sector's. NFI units rose 1.2 percent in regular trade and 1.5 in continuous trade, where the WIG 20 index gained 0.8 percent. -- Steven Silber +48 22 653 9700
